actual_shape_requirement.qualification: C0 position error alone does not bound curvature. Fixture, endpoint-axis, collet-exit strain transition, insulation, formed-wire equilibrium and the complete continuous actual centerline must be qualified against C1/C2 requirements. Actual material length must stay constant through withdrawal; eta1 is a reference-shape comparison, not permission to stretch wire. A point-cloud or position-tube check alone cannot pass this gate.
actual_shape_requirement.registration: q(s)=r(s)+e(s), with s the reference centerline arclength, including both straight tails and bridges. Require global C1 matching and piecewise C2 bounds, including transitions at both collet exits.

cut_and_preparation.scope: Lengths pay both bridges once and allow up to 1% C1 arclength growth of the entire new-wire path. Preparation is reserved outside that path, not available service slack. Existing main-cut qualification is an independent prerequisite; this study does not apply the new-wire shape certificate to main wires.

datums.derivation: Face gap [24.3,24.5] minus independently bounded anchor heights [1.95,2.05], plus continuous withdrawal through an actual stop in [10,10.1].
datums.scope: Proposed acceptance requirements, not supplier capabilities. XY offset and fixed tangent are reference values; residual position/tangent/shape errors require the complete C0/C1/C2 bound after datum registration. A common rigid transform does not affect curvature; it DOES affect obstacle clearance.

joined_budget.scope: Targets are stricter than existing global ceilings, charged once, with original hot-wire/contact/current assumptions. No realized copper extraction or new-main cut qualification is claimed.

reference_curve.method: 200 gap x 8 free-length x 512 curve cells. Cubic derivative/position boxes enclose the gap/handle rectangle; convex length in handle and negative Z derivative establish the positive rising root and its ordering. Handles have 1e-7 mm padding; arithmetic has 1e-9 padding. Floating engineering bounds, not certified directed interval arithmetic.
